rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 2 'Phase 2. Group synthesis' line 97: 'In the dry run, Claude dismissed "no time to experiment" as something that could not be addressed.' 'The dry run' never appears anywhere earlier in this file (never-named). It is not a session artifact of the reading student -- the reader has not run anything yet at this point in Phase 2, and the phrase does not match the session-artifact carve-out's shape (an artifact the student's OWN session just produced). Traced the referent: `curriculum/exercises/organisers-prepare-claude-basics.md` establishes a 'group-driver dry run' as an organiser rehearsal of this very exercise (lines 147 of that file), but that exercise is included only by `curriculum/trainings/claude-basics/organisers-run-the-workshop.md` -- a separate, organiser-only module from `where-is-this-all-going.md`, the module that includes find-the-crux.md (confirmed via `grep -rln` across curriculum/trainings/claude-basics/*.md). A student going through the student module never reads the organiser module, so the referent is never named anywhere in the material this reader holds -- not stranded by the re-chunk, ungrounded from the first read of the long-form file too. Harm the rule exists to prevent: a reader hits a pointer they cannot resolve and loses trust that the text means something concrete -- that harm is present here, since 'whose dry run, when' has no answer inside the student's reading path.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name it without requiring the organiser doc: e.g. 'When we tested this exercise, Claude dismissed...' or move the caution into the maintainer block as a note to facilitators.

'**Time:**' is corpus-wide template chrome, not a narrative choice by this file -- `grep -c "^\*\*Time:\*\*" curriculum/exercises/*.md | grep -v ":0" | wc -l` -> 40 of 41 exercise files open the same way, matching the rule's own principle that a budget cannot outrank a template that mandates the spend. Elsewhere in the file the only bold is the '**Prompt** *(Cowork...)*' caption preceding each fenced prompt (7 occurrences), the same fixed structural label used before every prompt fence across the corpus -- chrome, not narrative bold. resolution.note: check_slides §1 finding died on both lenses. Its traced antecedent was confabulated: the judge anchored 'the dry run' to the organiser rehearsal in organisers-prepare-claude-basics.md, a FUTURE per-cohort event a past-tense caution cannot refer to, and reachable only from the organiser-only module. The mechanical claim (one 'dry run' hit, no in-file antecedent) verified true and is the wrong test — the phrase is a plain-English noun, not a pronoun, demonstrative, or coined term needing an antecedent.
